statement: With a 12 percentage point first-line enrichment, shuffling within pages detected the injected effect in 80 of 100 synthetic texts at a one-sided 5% threshold. Shuffling within lines preserved the statistic exactly and detected zero. Without enrichment the page test rejected in 5 of 100. The size of the loss depends on the statistic and the resampling unit.
methods: Use independent Bernoulli tokens, with synthetic words p and o. Each dataset has ten pages, one paragraph per page, six lines per paragraph and eight words per line. Set P(p)=0.10 on all later lines and 0.10 plus delta on paragraph first lines. Test delta=0, 0.03, 0.06, 0.12, 0.24 across 100 synthetic text seeds. At each delta, for each integer seed 0..99, draw the 480 uniforms from Python random.Random('fleet-astra/K024/'+str(seed)) in page, line, token order. This pairs texts across the effect-size sweep.

Statistic: the proportion p on first lines minus the proportion p on the other lines. Compare it separately with the repo’s DSL shuffle_within_page and shuffle_within_line. Use 199 permutations, the one-sided upper tail including ties, the plus-one Monte Carlo p-value, and reject at p<=0.05. For each text reinitialize random.Random('fleet-astra/K024/null/'+str(seed)). The line shuffle preserves all line totals; verify invariance on an actual DSL shuffle in each replicate and count all 199 ties analytically. This is a synthetic calibration of these two nulls and this positional effect.
